incidents-bot: ALERT: Hosted API p99 latency spike detected in us-east1. GPU pool saturation + autoscaler errors. Queue depth rising > 12k requests. Error rate (504) increasing. Pager to SRE oncall.
Alice Nguyen: seeing the same in grafana — p95 jumped from 200ms -> 2.3s, p99 ~ 7s. backend queue length graph attached. A handful of clients showing timeouts.
Bob Patel: confirming. autoscaler logs show repeated CreateInstance failures: "quota_exceeded" + "rate_limit" from provisioner. Provisioner retries are backing off and queue is accumulating.
Charlie Ramos: ops-bot flagged several spikes from a single tenant (tenant-42) sending large batch requests; traffic pattern: sudden 20x burst of long-context generation (seq_len ~ 4k). Could be a bad client test.
Alice Nguyen: impact: approx 18% of requests now hit backend timeout, top customers affected: tenant-42, tenant-88, and some anonymous PLG calls. Cost SLOs not hit but customer SLAs may be.
Dana (sre-oncall): I'm on it. Taking lead. Quick wins: 1) enable emergency fallback routing to cpu-embed for low-priority requests; 2) throttle tenant-42; 3) open temporary dedicated pool if possible.
Bob Patel: agree. Trying to flip fallback policy now. Command: ```/runctl route set-policy hosted --fallback=smaller-quantized-v2 --match=priority<3``` 
Charlie Ramos: I'm escalating quota with cloud infra (request submitted). Also starting a concurrent drift-scan to find any stuck VMs preventing scale.
Alice Nguyen: can we push a short-lived rate-limiter at the edge to shed noisy tenants? We have existing route config for per-tenant qps caps.
Dana (sre-oncall): doing edge rule now. Applying rule to cap tenant-42 to 20 rps. Will post result.
ops-bot: ACTION: Applied edge rule: tenant-42 capped to 20rps. Old flows will be 429 for excess.
Bob Patel: fallback routing applied. Most non-critical requests now routing to smaller-quantized-v2. That reduced enqueue rate by ~40% for hosted queue.
Charlie Ramos: autoscaler: provisioning errors persisted due to API rate limits on the cloud account. I've switched to an alternate zone pool and started booting from spare images.
Alice Nguyen: metrics: queue depth down from 12k -> 6.2k in 8 minutes. p99 down to ~3.2s. Errors still ~6% but trending down.
Dana (sre-oncall): customer-impact note: we observed ~4k timed-out requests in last 15m. Escalating to support to notify top affected customers. Assigning postmortem: Charlie Ramos.
eng-runtime: FYI, we've enabled a KV-cache blacklist for tenant-42 sessions to avoid huge cache warmups expanding memory. Monitoring memory pressure.
Bob Patel: plan B if cloud quotas can't be raised quickly: fallback more aggressively to CPU for low-priority, and enable prefix-KV reuse to reduce compute per request.
Charlie Ramos: cloud admits a short window but expects quota bump in ~30 minutes. Meanwhile I'm manually spinning a small dedicated pool of 4 GPUs in alt zone to accept overflow.
Alice Nguyen: adding a synthetic probe to test the fallback path and confirm latency for non-critical responses.
ops-bot: NOTE: Emergency dedicated pool created (4xA10) in alt-us-east1-zone. Route rule added: overflow-route -> alt-pool.
Dana (sre-oncall): Handoff: I'm staying on until we confirm queue < 500 and p99 < 1s for 15m. If any regression, @Charlie Ramos please escalate.
Charlie Ramos: acknowledged. I'll stay for 1.5 hours and own the postmortem doc. Initial blameless summary: tenant-driven burst + cloud provisioner rate limits + autoscaler retry/backoff loop.
Bob Patel: short-term follow-ups: (1) tighten per-tenant default QPS caps; (2) add autoscaler circuit-breaker when CreateInstance errors hit threshold; (3) improve fallback routing latency tests.
Alice Nguyen: support notified customers and drafted incident comms. Will update status page with mitigation steps.
Dana (sre-oncall): status update in 30m or earlier if stabilized. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: queue depth 1h after root alert: 280 requests. p99 ~ 980ms. No new 504s. Monitoring.
Alice Nguyen: good to mark as monitoring. I'll keep the probe running and record metrics for postmortem.
Dana (sre-oncall): Incident moving to post-incident monitoring. Closing pager. Postmortem owner: Charlie Ramos. Timeline + actions to follow in the doc.
